title: Generate, compile, link
objective: Build blah in three steps: blah from blah.o, blah.o from blah.c, and a rule that creates blah.c itself.
hint: Work backwards from the goal: blah needs blah.o, blah.o needs blah.c, and the rule for blah.c has no prerequisites at all, so its recipe is the first one make runs.

steps.description: make starts at the deepest prerequisite and links last
steps.stdout:
echo "int main() { return 0; }" > blah.c # Runs first
cc -c blah.c -o blah.o # Runs second
cc blah.o -o blah # Runs third

steps.description: with every file in place there is nothing left to do

lesson.prediction: When building blah from an empty directory, what is the order of blah.c, blah.o, blah?
hints: The final goal blah depends on blah.o, and blah.o depends on blah.c.
Draw an arrow downward from the final goal and then execute it in the opposite direction.
lesson.explanation: Make recursively walks through the entire dependency chain, and then executes the recipe from the bottom.
